newsitem.title: USA: AIG to sell life insurance in Russia.
newsitem.headline: AIG to sell life insurance in Russia.

text.p: American International Group Inc said it expects to begin selling life insurance in Russia in the near future.
In addition, AIG said its American Life Insurance Co subsidiary launched life insurance operations in Egypt in a joint venture with a local partner in the third quarter.

AIG, which reported third quarter earnings on Thursday, said worldwide life insurance operations reported third quarter 1996 pretax income before realized gains of $328.7 million, an increase of 23.5 percent, compared to $266.1 million in 1995.
Premium income before the impact of foreign exchange rose 15.5 percent.
AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said all regions of the world contributed to the results.
He said life insurance operations in the United States, Latin America, Middle East and Central Europe all showed growth.
"As in the past, our major life operations in the Far East and Southeast Asia continued to do extremely well," Greenberg said in a statement.
Meanwhile, financial services also reported a strong quarter. AIG Financial Products Corp had a 62.7 percent increase in operating income.
International Lease Finance Corp reported a 17 percent gain and AIG Trading Group Inc rose over 100 percent.
AIG said its asset management businesses also continued to expand in the quarter.

"The U.S. property-casualty market remains very competitive for traditional coverages, and, as a result, AIG continues to focus on the specialty lines that have long been successful for us," AIG chairman Maurice Greenberg said in a prepared statement.
"We are aggressively pursuing opportunities in these classes, introducing new products that continue to fuel our domestic growth," he said.
AIG said worldwide premiums in general insurance rose 9.4 percent in the quarter before the impact of foreign exchange.
Domestic net premiums in general insurance rose 7.1 percent in the quarter and increased 12.7 percent excluding risk management business.
AIG said its overseas property-casualty business turned in a strong quarter, with net premiums written up 13.5 percent before the impact of foreign exchange.

The Far East, Southeast Asia, Europe and Latin America were all strong, AIG said. But in the United Kingdom, AIG said it faces the same competitive environment as in the United States and has consciously restricted its growth in areas that are underpriced.
